Starts in "headless mode" which allows using the application without user interface. This special mode can be used when the application is controlled by external clients via the API.
Notifies LibreOffice software that upon the creation of "UNO Acceptor Threads", a "UNO Accept String" will be used.
{file} macro://./[Library.Module.MacroName] Opens the file and applies specified macros from the file.
--pt {Printername} Prints the following files to the printer {Printername} and ends. The splash screen does not appear.
--print-to-file [--printer-name printer_name] [--outdir output_dir] Batch-print files to file.
--cat Applies filter "txt:Text" to the following text documents and dump text content to console (implies --headless).
--show[=N] Opens and starts the slideshow of the following presentation documents immediately.
--safe-mode Runs LibreOffice in troubleshoot mode, which temporarily replaces your user profile with a fresh one to help you diagnose and fix a faulty configuration.
--infilter=InputFilterName [:InputFilterParam[,param]] Forces an input filter type, if possible.
--view Opens following files in viewer mode (read-only).
-env:VAR[=VALUE] Set a bootstrap variable. For example, to set a non-default user profile path
--valgrind Automatically detect many memory management and threading bugs, and profile the program in detail.

LibreOffice provides unfettered access to our office productivity tools, at no cost to you.

Decades-long user relies on LibreOffice for real business and accounting work. Calc differs from Excel but handles nearly all the same tasks unless you're exchanging Excel-specific files in a corporate setting. Also runs it in Docker to generate PDFs from templates and normalize document formats.
Years-long user wants better table handling, e.g. pressing Tab in the last column should jump to the first column of the next row, as in MS Office.
Switched from SoftMaker to LibreOffice because LibreOffice supports LanguageTool, which SoftMaker's one-time-purchase version does not.
"Open source is great, but LibreOffice is a nightmare to use when you want to any actual work. I feel for the German bureaucrats."

WebAssembly build downloads about 300MB. One user found menus and text input worked in Chrome on Mac but were sluggish. In Safari on iPadOS/macOS it failed with 'Application exit (TypeError: Cannot convert "undefined" to int)'.

WASM version much slower than native on a 4300GE machine: the About window took ~5 seconds and scrolling lagged. Caching seemed not to work, so it re-downloaded and recompiled on reload. Another user found spell check had no dictionaries.
LibreOffice handled .docx projects that crashed MS Word, but the user wishes for a more modern UI; icons are too small and outdated.

Several users always use LibreOffice to edit CSVs because Excel alters them in unwanted ways. One said it opens CSVs without breaking them, though everything else about it is 'a slow, unintuitive mess.'
LibreOffice freezes on a new M4 Max MacBook Pro when exploring settings. Another Mac user wants to open files from within the app without granting full disk access.
Mother-in-law's old Word docs wouldn't format correctly in Office 365 on Win11. Installing LibreOffice rendered them correctly. Writer feels like Word 2000, so no relearning was needed.
Favorite underrated feature: editing PDFs directly at the object level with LibreOffice Draw.
Macro developer experience is poor: trying to fetch Jira ticket info with Basic and various Python APIs, the user gave up because simple automation became a nightmare.
Wrote a thesis in LibreOffice because the faculty didn't allow LaTeX, and was impressed by its features: 'It is a pro-tool.'

Base needs love: importing CSV meant copy-pasting cells from a spreadsheet, so the user went with DBeaver. Couldn't find docs for a JavaScript API for Calc. Draw was clunky. Writer is fine and does what you expect.
"It's horrible, incompatible, sluggish, slow and resources hog. Very bad UX. OnlyOffice is leaps and bounds better."
20-year user of LibreOffice/OpenOffice, mostly Impress for teaching, finds bugs, crashes and video issues very annoying and hasn't seen improvement. Would pay for an offline Linux alternative.
Periodically tries LibreOffice but returns to MS Office: noticeable lack of UI responsiveness, and large spreadsheet recalculation seemed 10x–100x slower.
Got a diesel repair shop to switch from MS Office to LibreOffice; 90% of work, including BOMs, labels, envelopes and invoices, now uses it. Says it 'runs like a scalded dog and never crashes.'
Tried LibreOffice Base as an Access alternative; it couldn't open an Access file or create a connection.
Commenter prefers OnlyOffice over LibreOffice for its more familiar interface and better MS Office compatibility: 'an electron app is better than native LibreOffice.'
